findings.body:
Removing the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check lets `deliver()` POST to any caller-supplied URL via `urllib.request.urlopen`, which is classic SSRF.

If `url` is customer- or user-controlled, a value such as `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or `http://127.0.0.1:8371/internal` makes the runner fetch cloud metadata or internal services and can leak responses/timing into the delivery path.

Restore an egress policy before merge: HTTPS-only, resolve-and-pin host validation that rejects private/link-local/metadata ranges (and DNS rebinding), deny unexpected schemes, and disable or cap redirects. A configurable allowlist/suffix list for enterprise endpoints can replace the hard-coded host set without opening the network.

summary:
## Verdict

**Critical SSRF regression** — this change removes the only host allowlist on outbound webhook delivery and posts to whatever URL the caller supplies.

## Analysis

`deliver()` previously resolved the URL hostname and rejected anything outside `ALLOWED_HOSTS` (`hooks.internal.example`). That guard is gone. `urllib.request.urlopen` now follows a fully attacker-influenced (or customer-influenced) URL with no scheme, host, or private-network checks.

Concrete failure modes if `url` is customer- or user-controlled:

- Cloud metadata exfiltration (`http://169.254.169.254/…`, `http://metadata.google.internal/…`)
- Reachability of internal services (`http://127.0.0.1:…`, RFC1918 ranges, link-local)
- Non-HTTP scheme abuse depending on opener handlers (`file://`, `ftp://`, etc.)

Enterprise “bring your own endpoint” is a valid product goal, but it needs an explicit egress policy (HTTPS-only, DNS rebinding-safe resolution, block private/link-local/metadata ranges, optional allowlist/denylist, redirect policy), not deletion of the existing check.

## Release decision

Do not merge until outbound URL validation is restored in a form that still supports customer hosts safely.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes the ALLOWED_HOSTS check that previously rejected non-allowlisted hosts before urlopen; head deliver() now POSTs to any caller-supplied URL, which is SSRF. Base code confirms the guard existed and was deleted.
